Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 

RECOMMENDED PARAMETERS OF 
STATIONARY STEAM BOILERS 



o 



1. Scope— -Covers the recommended. parameters for stationary steam boilers up to and including a 
maximum continuous rating of 25 tonnes/hour. The standard is not applicable for waste heat 
boilers and boilers for special purposes. 

2. Terminology — The definitions given in IS : 8595-1977 ' Terminology for parameters of stationary 
steam boilers ' are applicable. 

3. Recommended Parameters 

3.1 Maximum Continuous Rating (MCR) of Steam Boilers — The recommended values of the 
maximum continuous rating of steam boilers in tonnes/hour shall be as given below: 

1, 1*6, 2'5, 4'0, 6'3, (8), 10, 12'5, 16'0, 20'0, 25'0 
Note — Value given in parentheses is second preference value. 

3.2 Specified Pressure of Main Steam — The recommended values of specified pressure of main steam 
( gauge ) in mega pascals ( MPa ) shall be as given below: 

1, 1-6, 2'0 t 2'5, 3'2 t 4'0, 5*0 

3.3 Specified Temperature of Main Steam — The recommended values of specified temperature of 
main steam in °C are as follows: 

200, 250,315, 400 

Note — For saturated steam the saturation temperature shall apply. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

The quantities in this standard have been expressed in International System (SI) of units. 
However, for the sake of convenience the relative metric units and the corresponding conversion 



» factors are given below for general guidance: 



1 kgf/cm 3 = 98-066 5 kPa ( kilo Pascal ) = 0*098 066 5 MPa ( mega Pascal ) 

= 0-980 066 5 bar 
1 MPa - 10-1961 kgf/cm 2
